text:
anya: Quick sync — we need a decision on where retry/backoff and resume-token handling lives for the compact paginator across Python/TS/Go. Thinking: keep transport thin (network retry hooks) and let SDK own resume tokens + page logic. Pros/cons? cc @mike @jess @kevin

mike: +1 to SDK owning resume tokens. Transport should expose a minimal retry hook (error + attempt) but not invent or mutate tokens.

jess: SDK owning tokens is fine but it increases surface for Python/TS. For Go we prefer minimal allocations and explicit structs.

kevin: In TS we already have a retry hook shape. Proposal (example):
```ts
interface RetryPolicy {
  shouldRetry(err: Error, attempt: number): boolean;
  nextDelay(attempt: number): number;
}
```
SDK can compose token logic on top of that.

lina: Concern: if transport retries after a partial page fetch we can duplicate items unless resume token is authoritative and idempotent. Need a clear contract: when transport may retry vs when SDK must resume.

anya: Agreed. Proposal: transport retries only for network-level failures (connectivity, transient 5xx) and never for requests that might cause server-side side-effects unless the SDK supplied an opaque resume token. SDK is responsible for returning that resume token in responses and for replaying pages.

mike: That contract seems practical. Edge case: streaming endpoints vs paged endpoints. For streaming we probably let transport manage reconnect/resume where it understands streaming offsets; for paged endpoints SDK handles resume tokens.

jess: Implementation note: Python/TS can represent the opaque cursor as a base64 string. In Go we should keep it as []byte internally to avoid extra encoding/decoding on hot paths.

kevin: Also suggest a per-request override: `transportRetry: "none" | "standard" | "aggressive"` so callers can opt out or be more optimistic. Defaults to "standard" with jittered exponential backoff.

anya: Quick poll: are we ok with SDK owning resume tokens + page logic, and transport owning network-level retry hooks? React :thumbsup: for yes, :thinking_face: for objections.

mike: :thumbsup:

kevin: :thumbsup:

jess: :thinking_face: — worried about SDK surface complexity for beginners. Can we provide a super-simple default API that hides tokens most of the time?

anya: Yes — default high-level client will hide tokens and manage pagination automatically. Low-level client exposes cursor/token primitives for power users and for Go where we often need explicit control.

lina: One more: version the token envelope (e.g., `cursor_v1`) so we can change encoding/metadata later without breaking. Keep token semantics opaque to callers.

anya: Good point. We'll standardize `cursor_v1` format and add a migration path. I'll draft an RFC that includes: the transport retry hook shape, SDK token lifecycle, examples in Python/TS/Go, and the per-request override.

deploy-bot: Reminder: RFCs should be posted to the eng-platform RFC board and get at least 2 approvers before implementation.

anya: Thanks all — I'll post the RFC by Tue EOD with concrete code snippets and a short compat checklist. If anyone has strong objections, drop them here or DM me.
